newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia approves giant Busang gold deal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia approves giant Busang gold deal.

text.p: Indonesia on Tuesday approved a proposal from the small Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd to develop one of the world's biggest gold finds in the remote rainforests of Borneo island.
Bre-X's joint venture partner, U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold, will take the lead role in developing and operating the Busang deposit in East Kalimantan province.

Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana told a news conference tjat Alberta-based Bre-X had told his office the company had struck an equity deal with its Indonesian partners to develop the richest parts of the property.
"The general outline of the proposed share ownership is 55 percent for national (Indonesian government and local private) interests and 45 percent for Bre-X," he said.
He said the Indonesian interests had allocated a portion of their shares to Freeport McMoRan, amounting to 15 percent of the total.

"In holding to the principle that the government respects the application for a contract of work which has been approved in principle...the government accepts the proposal put foward by Bre-X and its Indonesian partners," he said.

The government endorsement of the deal closed a contentious chapter in Indonesia's mining sector that opened late last year when the Mines and Energy Ministry ordered Bre-X to partner Barrick Gold Corp in developing the Busang property.
Bre-X, which discovered the deposit, on Monday increased the estimated gold reserve in the find by 13.6 million ounces to 70.95 million ounces, currently worth more than $24 billion.
Barrick has given up the chase to partner Bre-X, informing the Indonesian government it would not reach an agreement with Bre-X although its offer was fair and equitable.
Under an earlier proposal announced by the ministry in December, Barrick was to take a 67.5 percent stake in Busang, Bre-X 22.5 and the government 10 percent.

Barrick had teamed up with a company controlled by President Syuharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardityanti Rukmana, while Bre-X had signed up a company controlled by the president's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, as a consultant.

Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh said on Monday the company had formed a joint venture with its Indonesian partners and Freeport, which operates one of the world's biggest copper and gold mines through Freeport Indonesia in Irian Jaya.
Its local partners include PT Askatindo Karya Minerals, which is 50-percent owned by the Nusamba group and the rest by the family of businessman Syakerani.

The Nusamba group is 80-percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto and 10-percent each by son Sigit and business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, a close friend and golfing partner of the president.
Another Indonesian partner, PT Amysa Lyna, is also equally owned by the Nusamba group and the Syakerani family.
Minister Sudjana said the government's approval of the deal was based on its satisfaction with the shares allocated to Indonesian interests.
"The development of the mineral resource, estimated to be quite large, will provide a significant contribution to national development, especially in eastern Indonesia," he said.
Sudjana also said state corporations would be given an opportunity to participate in the project when it enters the production stage, expected by industry sources in 2000.
"This is to reduce risks," he said. "In the meantime, the government hopes state companies will concentrate on exploration activities in areas under their jurisdiction."
